propers.name: Mandatum Antiphon 8
propers.text:
Ubi caritas et amor, Deus ibi est. V. Congregavit nos in unum Christi amor.
V. Exsultemus et in ipso jucundemur. V. Timeamus et amemus Deum vivum. V. Et
ex corde diligamus nos sincero. Et repetitur antiphona: Ubi caritas et amor,
Deus ibi est. V. Simul ergo cum in unum congregamur: V. Ne nos mente
dividamur, caveamus. V. Cessent jurgia maligna, cessent lites. V. Et in
medio nostri sit Christus Deus. Et repetitur antiphona: Ubi caritas et amor,
Deus ibi est. V. Simul quoque cum beatis videamus V. Glorianter vultum tuum,
Christe Deus: V. Gaudium, quod est immensum atque probum, V. Saecula per
infinita saeculorum. Amen.

translations.text:
Where are charity and love, God is there. V. The love of Christ hath gathered us together. V. Let us exult and be joyful in Him. V. Let us fear and love the living God. V. And let us love one another with sincere hearts.

Ant. Where are charity and love, God is there. V. Being, therefore, assembled together. V. Let us beware of being divided in mind. V. Let malicious upbraidings cease, let wranglings cease. V. And may Christ, our God, be in the midst of us.

Ant. Where are charity and love, God is there. V. Together with the blessed, too, may we see. V. Thy face in glory, O Christ, God. V. Which is infinitely noble joy. V. Through endless ages of ages. Amen.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after `Domine` and none after `et` (`et quia tu`); 1962 sets both; 1862 sets a comma after `hic nobis`; 1962 does not; CONCLUSION LENGTH: 1862 `qui vivis et regnas Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum`; 1962 `qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum`. The 1862's is the longer form here -- the usual direction is reversed.; 1862 layer damage: `aespi-cias` for `despicias` (line 31897) and `interioria` for `interiora` (line 31903); letterforms inferred, not read. Corroboration: 1604 at line 26802 prints `...irum interiora lauentur peccata. Quod ipse praestare digneri[s]...` (long s as f/i throughout, u for v), which supplies `interiora laventur peccata` at the same place and disposes of the 1862 layer's `interioria`. Recorded limitation: Confidence is medium only because two words (`despicias`, `interiora`) were inferred from damaged letterforms rather than read; the 1604 supplies the second at the same point in the same prayer. The conclusion difference is a length difference in one rubrical formula (`qui vivis et regnas ...`), not a different formula, so it stays inside the pilot's settled tolerance. The 1862 prints this prayer after the Mandatum performed AFTER Mass and after the stripping of the altars; the 1955 rite moves the Mandatum inside Mass after the homily. Placement moved; the words did not.

propers.name: Prayer of the Mandatum
propers.text:
Adesto, Domine, quaesumus, officio servitutis nostrae: et, quia tu
discipulis tuis pedes lavare dignatus es, ne despicias opera manuum tuarum,
quae nobis retinenda mandasti: ut, sicut hic nobis et a nobis exteriora
abluuntur inquinamenta; sic a te omnium nostrum interiora laventur peccata.
Quod ipse praestare digneris, qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. R.
Amen.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text:
Be present, Lord, we ask, in the duty of our service; and because you deigned to wash your disciples' feet, do not disdain the works of your hands, which you commanded us to keep, so that, just as outward stains are washed away here for us and by us, so the inward sins of us all may be washed away by you. May you yourself be pleased to grant this, you who live and reign for ages of ages.
R. Amen.

propers.name: Hymn at the Translation of the Blessed Sacrament
propers.text:
Dum fit processio, cantatur hymnus Pange, lingua, gloriosi Corporis
mysterium, usque ad verba Tantum ergo; si vero opus sit, idem hymnus
repetitur.

Pange, lingua, gloriosi
Corporis mysterium,
Sanguinisque pretiosi,
Quem in mundi pretium,
Fructus ventris generosi,
Rex effudit gentium.

Nobis datus, nobis natus
Ex intacta Virgine,
Et in mundo conversatus,
Sparso verbi semine,
Sui moras incolatus
Miro clausit ordine.

In supremae nocte coenae
Recumbens cum fratribus,
Observata lege plene
Cibis in legalibus,
Cibum turbae duodenae
Se dat suis manibus.

Verbum caro, panem verum
Verbo carnem efficit:
Fitque sanguis Christi merum:
Et si sensus deficit,
Ad firmandum cor sincerum
Sola fides sufficit.

Tantum ergo Sacramentum
Veneremur cernui:
Et antiquum documentum
Novo cedat ritui:
Praestet fides supplementum
Sensuum defectui.

Genitori, Genitoque
Laus et jubilatio,
Salus, honor, virtus quoque
Sit et benedictio:
Procedenti ab utroque
Compar sit laudatio.
Amen.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text:
During the procession, the hymn Pange lingua, gloriosi Corporis mysterium is sung as far as the words Tantum ergo; if needed, the same hymn is repeated.

Tongue, proclaim the mystery
of the glorious Body
and of the precious Blood
which, as the ransom of the world,
the King of the nations,
the fruit of a noble womb, poured out.

Given to us, born for us
from an undefiled Virgin,
and having lived in the world,
after sowing the seed of the word,
he brought his time of dwelling here
to a close in a wondrous order.

During the night of the final supper,
reclining among his brothers,
having fully observed the law
in the foods that the law required,
he gives himself with his own hands
as food for the company of twelve.

The incarnate Word makes real bread
into flesh by his word;
the pure wine becomes Christ's Blood.
If the senses fall short,
faith alone is sufficient
to make the sincere heart firm.

Therefore, let us bow in reverence
before so great a Sacrament.
Let the ancient observance
yield to the new rite;
may faith supply
what our senses lack.

To the Father and to the Son
be praise and joyful acclaim,
salvation, honor, power,
and blessing as well;
to the One who proceeds from both
let equal praise be given.
Amen.
